duplicate_gate.selected_construct: NMOSD optic neuritis + longitudinally extensive myelitis + area postrema syndrome

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Relapsing optic-spinal disease with a long cord lesion, area-postrema symptoms and detected AQP4-IgG reconstructs NMOSD.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: MOGAD can mimic optic neuritis and longitudinal myelitis; the original version was therefore strengthened with AQP4-IgG. After correction, NMOSD is uniquely best.
adversarial_second_pass.MS_attack: The lesion length, area-postrema syndrome and AQP4-IgG argue strongly against conventional MS.
adversarial_second_pass.ADEM_attack: No encephalopathy or monophasic multifocal postinfectious syndrome.
adversarial_second_pass.infarct_attack: A spinal infarct does not explain the separated optic-neuritis episode and AQP4 autoimmunity.
adversarial_second_pass.correction_check: Fresh post-correction duplicate scan remained zero-hit.
